# 0.3.0 - RX-V1900 support and a new user guide

This release adds RX-V1900 profiles, corrects playback format and sampling
rate on the RX-Vx700 and RX-Vx800 profiles, frees ESP8266 RAM, and rewrites
the user documentation around the RX-V1600 reference receiver.

## Highlights

- `rx_v1900` and `rx_v1900_extended` profiles, contributed in #14 and tested
  on one RX-V1900 G/E (UK/Europe) unit. `auto` selects the extended profile
  when the receiver reports DC2 model ID `R0240`. The profile has its own
  input, DSP program and System Memory (1-6) lists, reads zone 2, tuner and
  playback state from the startup DC2 reply, and adds a `surround_decoder`
  select for Pro Logic, PLII and Neo:6. Commands the RX-V1900 does not have or
  ignores (Speaker A/B, the sleep timer, the Auto/DTS/AAC decoder mode) are
  rejected before they are sent, so they cannot time out and mark the
  receiver unavailable.
- RX-Vx700, RX-Vx800 and RX-V1900 decode playback format and sampling rate
  with the RX-Vx700 RS-232C tables and the full report byte: `04`/`09` is now
  Dolby Digital at 48 kHz, not "Dolby Digital 2.0" at 176.4 kHz. RX-Vx500 and
  RX-Vx600 are unchanged.
- DC2 input decoding is per profile. DC4 setup writes that the receiver
  acknowledges with a bare status and no value echo, as the RX-V1900 does for
  bass and treble, are accepted instead of timing out.
- Error messages and lookup tables stay in flash on the ESP8266. The full
  example uses 38,324 bytes of static RAM instead of 45,240 (15.3% less);
  flash rises from 487,772 to 494,140 bytes. These are linker measurements on
  the pinned build baseline, not runtime heap figures.
- A new user guide. The README is a short quick start;
  [Configuration](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.3.0/docs/configuration.md)
  describes every option and entity;
  [Supported Receivers](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.3.0/docs/supported_models.md)
  shows which entities each profile supports and gives a configuration per
  receiver; [Wiring](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.3.0/docs/wiring.md)
  has the pins of each example.
- `receiver_reset` and `dc3:reset` are documented as the factory reset they
  are: the receiver deletes every user setting. The full example disables the
  button by default.

## Upgrade Notes

- No option was renamed or removed; `v0.2.4` configurations keep working.
- `examples/` holds only RX-V1600 configurations.
  `examples/yamaha_rx_vx500.yaml` moved into Supported Receivers, without the
  reset button and with raw commands off.
- On RX-Vx700 and RX-Vx800, the playback format and sampling rate text
  changes. Update automations that match the old text.
- RX-V1900 owners: set `model: "RX-V1900"`, keep `receiver_profile: auto`,
  drop an `inputs:` block copied from the RX-V1600 examples, and set
  RS-232C STANDBY to YES on the receiver.
- Read [Maintenance and Migration](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.3.0/docs/maintenance.md#migration)
  before upgrading.

## Validation and Limits

The build baseline remains ESPHome 2026.10.1, with HA companion runtime tests
on Home Assistant 2026.10.4. CI covers Python 3.12-3.14, production C++ tests
and fuzzing with sanitizers, all ten explicit profiles, minimum ESPHome
configuration validation, the receiver configurations shown in the docs, and
ESP32/ESP8266 firmware builds with size budgets.

The host dependency pins are unchanged from `0.2.4`, so the known
host-dependency vulnerabilities remain: stable ESPHome pins Pillow 12.3.0 and
filelock 4.0.10, and the HA test baseline also pins Pillow 12.3.0. These Python
packages are not embedded in the ESP firmware. See the
[Security Policy](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/v0.3.0/SECURITY.md)
for exposure reductions and the remaining limitations. This release is not
declared vulnerability-free.

No firmware or HA integration is installed automatically. Apart from the
RX-V1900 unit above, no new hardware validation is claimed; RX-V1900 regional
variants (U/C/J) and the RX-Vx700 and RX-Vx800 profiles still need real-device
testing. Source and sound-mode selection in the receiver media player still
needs the optional HA companion.
